description: Create house.item, the supertype every physical thing in the house is a row of.
rationale: Every category shares four facts -- what it is called, what it cost, when it was bought and which room it is in -- and nothing else does. Putting them in one table means 'what did the house cost' is one query instead of a seven-way UNION, and each detail table then carries only what makes its category different.

intents.comment: One physical thing in the house. The category column says which detail table carries the rest of it.

columns.name: item_id
columns.comment: Surrogate key. The detail tables use this same value as their own primary key.

columns.name: category
columns.comment: Which detail table extends this row. Immutable in practice: a chair does not become a saucepan.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: What the household calls this thing.

columns.name: brand_id
columns.comment: Maker, where there is one. Null for anything hand-made or unbranded.

columns.name: room_id
columns.comment: Room the thing is in. Null while it is in transit, lent out, or nobody has looked.

columns.name: purchase_date
columns.comment: When it was bought. Required: an item nobody can date is an item nobody can depreciate.

columns.name: purchase_price
columns.comment: What was paid, in the household currency. Zero is legal and means a gift.

columns.name: current_price
columns.comment: What it would fetch today. Null until somebody values it; 0095 fills the first estimate.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.comment: When this row was last changed. Maintained by the house.touch_updated_at trigger.

intents.name: item_category_purchase_date_idx
intents.comment: The inventory screen lists one category, newest purchase first.

intents.name: item_brand_id_idx
intents.comment: Leads with the referencing column of item_brand_fk, so deleting a brand does not scan house.item.

intents.name: item_room_id_idx
intents.comment: Leads with the referencing column of item_room_fk, and serves 'everything in this room'.
